security_spec.violation_condition: On RV64, the kernel (as host supervisor or TVM manager) passes a non-zero _hi address parameter to any CoVE-IO SBI function whose spec now mandates _hi must be zero on RV64. The TSM may interpret a non-zero _hi as the upper bits of a wider physical address, causing it to read/write memory outside the intended region.
security_spec.summary: Unvalidated _hi address parameters on RV64 permit crafted physical addresses to redirect TSM memory accesses outside intended regions, enabling data corruption or information leak through the TSM

findings.finding: No CoVE-IO SBI code exists in this kernel tree. grep for SBI_EXT_COVE, COVE_IO, cove_io, cove-vio across the entire codebase returned zero matches. The SBI extension IDs in arch/riscv/include/asm/sbi.h do not include any CoVE extension. There is no code that could pass a non-zero _hi address to any CoVE-IO SBI function, so the spec violation condition cannot be triggered. The kernel is compliant by default.

SBI STA (not CoVE-IO) already demonstrates the correct pattern: on RV64, a non-zero shmem_phys_hi returns SBI_ERR_INVALID_ADDRESS. This is exactly the behavior the CoVE-IO spec would require — rejecting non-zero _hi on RV64 rather than silently interpreting it as upper address bits.

SBI PMU snapshot (not CoVE-IO) demonstrates the identical correct pattern: non-zero saddr_high on RV64 returns SBI_ERR_INVALID_ADDRESS. This pattern is already established in the KVM SBI handling code for address pair parameters.

Guest-side SBI STA steal-time setup (not CoVE-IO) correctly computes hi=0 on RV64 via IS_ENABLED(CONFIG_32BIT) before passing to SBI. This is the correct pattern for guest-side callers: on RV64, _hi should always be 0 when the physical address fits in 32 bits (which is always true for __pa() on a per-CPU variable).
